subject: ACME - pricing & invoice estimate follow-up
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Meyers <jordan.m@acme.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: ACME discovery recap + numbers we discussed

Hi Jordan / Procurement team —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from my side and a few asks so we can pull together a formal invoice estimate and cost model: 

Recap:
- Primary use: contextual search + assistant for support flow (user prompts -> model responses, some reranking)
- Expected traffic: you mentioned a baseline and potential spike window (details below)
- Requirement: US + EU serving, optional dedicated/reserved capacity for predictable spikes

Asks to finalize the estimate:
1) Monthly token volumes (baseline vs peak) — please provide current monthly avg and a 6–12 month forecast if available.
2) Target unit economics — what is your target $/1M tokens or target monthly budget range?
3) Typical request size: avg prompt + response token length (helps with KV cache and batching assumptions)
4) Any required retention, audit log retention length, or specific compliance needs beyond SOC 2 (affects Private offering/per-seat costs)

I attached a quick pricing calculator (acme_pricing_calc_v1.xlsx) and our unit-cost breakdown (summary PDF) to show assumptions we typically use. When you send volumes and target budget, I’ll produce: a) hosted estimate, b) dedicated reserved option (1-year commit) with discount schedule, and c) a cost model showing unit economics and where savings come from (batching, KV cache, quantization).

Next steps: if you can send the volumes and target $/1M by end of day tomorrow I’ll have a formal estimate ready for review by Thursday. Also happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the model. 

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: acme_pricing_calc_v1.xlsx, redwood_unit_cost_breakdown.pdf

From: Jordan Meyers <jordan.m@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME discovery recap + numbers we discussed

Thanks Sean — good recap. One correction: we also plan to do nightly batch reranks which will increase downstream token counts (included below). Here are the numbers from Finance/Analytics: 

Volumes:
- Current baseline (monthly): ~150,000,000 tokens/month
- Expected sustained growth (6 months): 200–250M/month
- Peak/spike (marketing campaign windows): up to ~500,000,000 tokens/month (for 2–4 weeks at a time)

Request size:
- Average end-to-end (prompt + response + rerank work): ~1,200 tokens/request

Budget / unit target:
- Finance is targeting roughly $110 / 1M tokens as a target unit economics number for hosted API (we can flex up to $140/1M if the performance and SLAs justify it)
- Monthly budget band we can sign off on: $15,000 — $65,000 depending on the quarter and campaign cadence

Compliance:
- SOC 2 Type II is sufficient for now. We will surface PCI/PHI needs later if needed.

Attached: acme_current_volume_report.csv (monthly export)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: ACME discovery recap + numbers we discussed (internal)

Sean / Marissa — thanks for looping me in. Quick internal notes based on Jordan’s numbers: 

- Baseline 150M @ $110/1M -> ~$16.5k/mo; peak 500M -> ~$55k/mo (hosted).
- Opportunity: 1-year reserved could likely get to ~$85/1M with commit + auto-scaling burst. That would put baseline ~12.75k/mo and peak ~42.5k/mo — within their $15k–$65k band for many quarters.
- Need to model multi-region (US + EU) egress and regional latency nodes; include a line item for EU footprint (~+12% on infra cost)
- List assumptions explicitly in the cost model: avg tokens/request, KV cache hit rate (assume 20% for now), batching efficiency (assume 1.8x), quantization savings (if they accept int8).

Action items for Sean:
1) Produce formal invoice estimate with two scenarios: Hosted (pay-as-you-go) vs Dedicated Reserved (1-year) — include monthly and annualized totals.
2) Attach cost_model_breakdown.pdf and the ACME invoice spreadsheet.
3) Call/meeting to review — aim for Thu or Fri.

I’ll help QA the estimates before we send to Jordan/procurement.

-Rachel
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Meyers <jordan.m@acme.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME - formal invoice estimate and cost model (attached)

Jordan / Procurement — attaching the formal estimate and a short cost model summary as requested. Highlights below and assumptions called out so your finance team can reconcile quickly.

Summary (monthly):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go) @ $110 / 1M tokens (unit target you provided)
  • Baseline 150M tokens = $16,500 / month
  • Sustained growth (250M) = $27,500 / month
  • Peak 500M = $55,000 / month

- Dedicated (1-year reserved) suggested pricing tiers: 
  • Tier A (85 / 1M tokens) w/ 1-year commit, burst capacity: 
    - Baseline 150M = $12,750 / month
    - Peak 500M = $42,500 / month
  • We also modeled a 2x burst buffer for 2 weeks (additional charge only if used)

Key assumptions included in attachments (ACME_invoice_estimate_20270721.xlsx and cost_model_breakdown.pdf):
- Avg tokens/request: 1,200
- KV cache hit rate: 20%
- Batching efficiency: 1.8x on average
- EU footprint adds ~12% infra line item
- No additional compliance charges beyond SOC 2 in the current estimate

Attachments: ACME_invoice_estimate_20270721.xlsx, cost_model_breakdown.pdf

Next steps:
1) Review with Procurement — would a 30-min review tomorrow at 11am PT work?
2) If procurement is comfortable, we’ll prepare a formal quote and a DocuSign for a 1-year reserved commitment option.
3) If you’d like, we can include a short POC period (30 days) to validate perf at baseline before committing to reserved capacity.

Let me know which option you prefer and whether Finance would like the invoice split by region.

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
